title: AI use is up, but worker training is falling behind: report
summary: Effective AI training starts with experimentation, not tools, experts say While artificial intelligence (AI) adoption is accelerating across workplaces, access to the training and resources meant to support it is falling — and for many workers, that gap is starting to show, according to a new global report. AI use among workers rose 10 percentage points year over year, with nearly two-thirds (64 per cent) of the workforce now using it at work.

title: 1 in 3 young Canadians use AI once a month for mental health, report shows
summary: One in three young Canadians, say they regularly use generative AI tools at least once a month to support their mental health, a new survey said on Friday. Young Canadians are leaning more on generative artificial intelligence tools for mental health support, a new report says. One in three young Canadians, say they regularly use generative AI tools at least once a month to try to support their mental health, a survey by Canadian mental health network Jack.org said on Friday. Among those who use these tools, nearly half say they have not shared their use of AI chatbots for mental health with anyone. Three out of five said they use these tools to navigate specific situations, most commonly social relationships including friendships, romantic relationships, and family dynamics.

title: AI’s leaders (probably) aren’t faking their fear
summary: When tech CEOs say their products might kill us all, are they trying to sell us something? Silicon Valley has long warned that its favorite technology might get us all killed. But chatter about AI’s apocalyptic potential has grown louder in recent weeks. In September, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from the company, accusing his former employer of “gambling with our lives” by developing evermore powerful models faster than it could control them. One of Coxon’s former colleagues vouched for this assessment, saying that there was a greater than 10 percent chance of AI “killing all humans” within the next decade.

title: Halton Regional Police uses AI in hiring, training 911 call takers
summary: Halton regional police in Ontario are using artificial intelligence in the recruitment and training of 911 call takers and dispatchers. The force said American AI firm GovWorx provides the technology to create emergency call simulations to help 911 applicants improve their decision-making, communication and crisis management skills. Halton police 911 communications bureau manager Brian Dodd said the new technology helps the force identify the right candidates from the beginning of the hiring process.

title: OpenAI to bring in $20 billion less than previously expected
summary: Investors expected more. According to a new report from the Financial Times , OpenAI has informed investors that the company is expected to make $50 billion in revenue for the year. That's a lot of money, but it's also a full $20 billion less than earlier projections from just last month, which predicted the company would earn $70 billion in annual revenue. AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are in the midst of an unprecedented infrastructure spending spree, with the AI industry spending trillions on data centers and other resources. And as CNN noted , the Financial Times' report could "rattle investors" worried that these companies won't be able to turn a profit after all.

title: Prize-winning image which sparked backlash was AI-generated, Nikon rules
summary: The camera-maker says it is now re-evaluating the rules and procedures of its Small World in Motion contest. The winner of a prestigious scientific photography competition has been disqualified following concerns raised by other scientists that it was fake. Nikon said the use of generative AI in the composition of the video broke the rules of its Small World In Motion contest, which accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes. The firm said the video "did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI", but added it was not a judgement of the entrant's professional reputation or scientific contributions.
